title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police falsely charged her with bank theft. She spent nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records proving she was in Tennessee when the fraud occurred, and she was released on Christmas Eve with no way home.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10 million, claiming police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video without doing further investigation. The lawsuit says she lost her home, car, and belongings, was denied medications and dentures, and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The suit seeks accountability and hopes to encourage more careful police use of facial recognition technology.
